03 / Module 1 • Energy strategy

CNG addresses a trilemma — not a single price

Affordability, availability and accountability have to be delivered together.

Nigeria Energy Transition Plan
₦

Affordability

Post-subsidy petrol/diesel price volatility transmits into household transport costs, wage pressure and business logistics.

◫

Availability

A cheaper energy source does not help the commuter if stations are distant, queues are long or vehicles lack reliable installation and servicing.

✓

Accountability

Conversion subsidies, duty waivers, station assets and fare savings need traceable beneficiaries, records and objective verification.

The transition-fuel thesis — with boundaries

  • Gas can displace some imported liquid-transport-fuel exposure and support domestic value addition.
  • Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan explicitly treats gas as a transition resource, with overall demand rising towards 2030 and falling later on the path to 2060.
  • Methane leakage, lifecycle emissions and fossil-asset lock-in must be included in the appraisal; “gas” is not the same as “zero carbon”.

Nigeria Energy Transition Plan: natural gas

Presenter cue. Differentiate 'CNG is cheaper' from 'CNG delivered at the right route, uptime and safety'. Discuss emissions without calling CNG a renewable fuel.

Formula: monthly km = km/day × working days; displaced-fuel saving = route share × [km × petrol price / petrol efficiency − km × CNG price / CNG efficiency]; net recurring savings = displaced saving − incremental maintenance. Project NPV discounts 36 monthly savings against upfront kit capex and conversion downtime. No terminal proceeds, tax, grants, financing cash flows or escalation are included. Prices and efficiencies are illustrative — NOT market quotes.

Presenter cue · 12 minutes. Invite the room to change station access from 90% to 50%. Compare simple payback to discounted value. EY strategy and assurance colleagues should challenge both the baseline and the underlying data.
07 / Project finance workshop

Can a CNG refuelling station earn its cost of capital?

Stations depend on utilisation, take-or-pay demand, energy costs, margins and debt coverage — not just installed capacity.

Station-side assumptions • illustrative

Annual trading viability

Annual EBITDA proxy
—
Simple capex recovery
—
Debt-service coverage proxy
—
Min. utilisation for target DSCR
—
Assumptions shown for workshop only.

Investment committee test

  1. Are 12-month route volumes committed by anchor fleets?
  2. What happens to compression power, feed-gas price and trucked CNG supply costs?
  3. Can station throughput and payment data be reconciled to the kilogram/SCM?
  4. Is the debt profile resilient to downtime, FX and demand shortfall?

Annual station EBITDA proxy = capacity × utilisation × days × unit contribution margin − fixed OPEX. DSCR proxy = EBITDA ÷ scheduled annual debt service (not CFADS and not a credit-approved DSCR). Required utilisation solves EBITDA ≥ target DSCR × debt service. Depreciation, taxes, working capital, renewals, financing fees, VAT and debt covenants are excluded.

Presenter cue · 7 minutes. Put utilisation at 35%. Ask whether a subsidy on capex alone is sufficient without contracted offtake. Demonstrate sensitivity of DSCR.
08 / Risk-adjusted decision

What the investment committee must challenge

Headline discounts are not a substitute for resilient cashflows, safe operations or documentary safeguards.

Demand / operational risk

  • Station proximity and queues
  • Offtake minimums versus spot sales
  • Reconversion, safety and warranty concerns
  • Availability, weather and maintenance

Finance / macro risk

  • Imported equipment FX and customs costs
  • Borrowing costs and tenor mismatch
  • Energy price-spread compression
  • Counterparty and government-payment delays

Legal / reputational risk

  • Unsafe or uncertified installation
  • Ineligible duty / VAT claims
  • Unsubstantiated savings / emissions
  • Privacy, cyber and beneficiary misuse

Risk heatmap • click a pressure point

Executive decision gate

GO → CONDITIONAL GO → DEFER

Use measurable conditions: verified energy cost advantage, approved kit and incentive documents, adequate station coverage, credible downside cash flows and independently monitored safety.

Presenter cue. Ask one group to recommend proceeding; the other must challenge approval on supply, model robustness and financial reporting.
09 / Module 3 • Nigerian fiscal dimensions

Tax policy creates value — only when the legal conditions are met

Separate statutory provisions, ministerial orders, programme announcements and client-specific approvals. The 2026 framework requires period-sensitive analysis.

IssuePosition to testEY professional action
Nigeria Tax Acts 2025Federal transition guidance identifies 1 January 2026 commencement for the Nigeria Tax Act, with legacy periods under the repealed rules.Map transaction date, accounting period, incentives and transitional documentation.
Fossil-fuel surchargeThe legislation contains a 5% charge and explicit CNG exclusion. Administration starts by ministerial Gazette order — do not assert blanket collection from 1 January.Obtain enacted text plus applicable commencement order; classify products precisely.
CNG / EV duty and VAT waiversPi-CNG announced August 2026 waivers for eligible vehicles, tricycles and related components. Not every import or downstream service automatically qualifies.Document scope, effective dates, IDEC/approvals, customs tariff line and VAT supply class.
VAT suspension and classificationTax Act provisions contemplate ministerial scheduling/classification for CNG and related equipment; treatment can differ between CNG, kits, conversion services and invoices.Obtain operative Gazette notice and written product-by-product tax position.
2026 vehicle green tax2026 fiscal-policy measures address specified engine-size bands, including exceptions. CNG conversion alone does not prove an exemption.Evaluate tariff schedule, mass-transit status, engine capacity and date of import.

Sources: Finance Ministry, June 2026 · Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 · Pi-CNG policy notice · Tax summaries, reviewed May 2026

Legal interpretation safeguard: Treat this as a professional issue-spotting framework, not a tax ruling or representation that a proposed import qualifies. Verify the latest legal instrument and applicable approvals.
Presenter cue · 10 minutes. Differentiate legal provision, effective commencement and actual administrative implementation. Invite tax staff to explain how a ministerial order changes operational VAT and surcharge conclusions.

11 / Assurance & financial reporting

Where CNG programmes enter the financial statements

From conversion kits to station assets and grants: recognition and measurement must follow substance.

IAS 16 / IAS 36

Station construction, compressors, qualifying conversion installations, componentisation, useful lives, residual values and impairment triggers.

IAS 20

Government assistance, free/subsidised kits, grant conditions and reasonable assurance. Consider grant presentation and matching.

IFRS 15 / IFRS 16

Conversion services, station fuel sales, contracts, bundled services, customer rebates, leases and identified-asset arrangements.

IAS 37

Warranty obligations, provisions, remediation and onerous station supply or installation contracts where recognition conditions are met.

IFRS 9 / IAS 12

Receivable expected credit losses, financing instruments, government counterparties, deferred-tax consequences and recoverability.

ESG disclosure

Establish robust base-year methodology; report fuel substitution and credible GHG estimates without treating CNG as zero-emissions.

Accountant’s golden rule: Asset funded by government ≠ nil accounting asset automatically; project labelled 'green' ≠ non-impairment. Financial statement treatment turns on the actual contractual rights, obligations, conditions and measurement criteria.
Presenter cue · 9 minutes. Ask assurance professionals to identify which judgments would move an EBITDA, cash flow or impairment result materially.

13 / Future-ready accountant

Digitise the evidence, not merely the dashboard

Data integrity is the bridge between physical gas delivery, financial reporting and credible transport relief.

Six connected data sources

Vehicle IDunique registry
Kit IDinstallation
Dispensing datameter • SCM
PaymentsPOS/bank
Route / GPSkm • uptime
Inspectioncertification

Reconcile transactions at the vehicle–kit–station–route level. Run exception detection for duplicates, unusual volumes, impossible mileage, mismatched payments and expired inspections.

Live fraud/anomaly teaching scenario

1One kit serial number appears on three vehicle records.
2Reported SCM consumption is 2.4× a vehicle’s expected range.
3Station cash sales exceed metered volume-based revenue.
4A retired vehicle continues receiving government-supported refills.

Digital controls architecture

  • Asset master-data governance and identity verification
  • Maker–checker on beneficiary creation and kit assignment
  • Signed dispenser logs, tamper alerts and calibration history
  • Daily station → payment → bank reconciliation
  • Role-based access, API assurance, backups and incident reporting

AI caveat

AI cannot certify a false input. Analytical flags require investigation, while model drift, fairness, privacy and false positives require governance.

Digital assurance should be designed from procurement to impact verification, not bolted on after public reporting.

Presenter cue. Poll: What is your highest-priority control if one kit can generate multiple subsidies? Let tax, IT audit and assurance perspectives differ.
14 / Stewardship and public trust

CNG is lower-carbon potential, not a green blank cheque

Transport-energy transition claims need baseline methodology, safety design and evidence from the field.

Safety-critical controls

  • Certified kit specification and technician competency
  • Cylinder integrity and inspection schedule
  • Pressure limits, safety valves and leak tests
  • Insurance, incident response and recall procedure

Environmental methodology

  • Quantify kilometre baseline and energy conversion factors
  • Account for upstream methane and lifecycle boundary
  • Capture real fuel volume, downtime and route conditions
  • Disclose assumptions and avoid zero-emission claims

Social outcome test

  • Are the intended beneficiaries actually riding?
  • What routes and time windows are covered?
  • Are fare reductions financially durable?
  • Who absorbs conversion and operating subsidies?

Board-level ESG measures

Active converted vehicles • verified kilometres • SCM dispensed • station uptime • incident rate • overdue inspections • estimated lifecycle emissions • subsidy per verified passenger trip • fares relative to baseline.

Reporting principle: Define method, boundary, baseline, source records, assurance level and uncertainty.
Presenter cue. Explain the difference between measuring tailpipe emissions and a complete lifecycle assessment. Emphasise chain-of-custody evidence.

16 / State-sector advisory lens

Does lower fleet fuel cost actually lower passenger fares?

Case: official 19 September update cited Borno fares of ₦50–₦100 against commercial ₦300–₦600 on selected routes.

Evidence or attribution?

A lower observed fare is an outcome, but it may also reflect fleet subsidies, donated buses, capped tariffs, fuel cross-subsidy, route allocation or public funding. It does not independently prove that CNG alone caused the difference.

ClaimVerification evidence
Passengers paid lessTimestamped tickets, routes, comparator fares, sampling
CNG drove the changeFuel consumption, full cost bridge and subsidy allocation
Benefit is scalableUtilisation, station throughput, route demand, public cashflow
Benefit is sustainableMaintenance, full-life capex, fares and funding agreements

Public-sector scorecard

Transport fare per passenger-km versus route baseline
Total public subsidy per verified passenger trip
Bus availability and kilometres in revenue service
Station SCM dispensed and fleet consumption reconciliation
Vehicle safety incidents, inspections and missed services
Independent passenger feedback and complaints closure

Source for the quoted Borno figures: Presidential statement dated 19 September 2026. These are official reported examples, not independent impact evaluation.

Presenter cue. Pose the counterfactual: 'What if buses were free and fares were fixed?' This separates gross programme effect from fuel saving.

THE FUTURE-READY CHARTERED ACCOUNTANT

Make CNG policy investable, compliant, auditable and sustainable.

Our responsibility is not to celebrate a cheaper fuel narrative; it is to demonstrate that the economics endure, the incentives are defensible, the risks are controlled and the savings are real.

Three boardroom tests

Money: What are the real lifetime cash flows?

Evidence: Can an independent reviewer reproduce them?

Impact: Who truly benefits, and how do we know?
